subject: math
title: Compare Two-Digit Numbers
seo_title: Grade 1 Comparing Two-Digit Numbers Worksheets: Greater Than, Less Than and Equal To
domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
standard_text: Compare two two-digit numbers based on meanings of the tens and ones digits, recording the results of comparisons with the symbols >, =, and <.
meta_desc: Free 1st grade comparing numbers worksheets: compare two-digit numbers with tens and ones blocks, use the >, < and = symbols with the alligator trick, find the greatest and least, and solve word problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Look at the tens first. If the tens are the same, compare the ones.
key_sub: 31 > 29, because 3 tens is more than 2 tens. The open mouth of > and < faces the greater number.
body_html:
Tens are worth more than ones

A two-digit number has tens and ones. One ten is the same as 10 ones. So the tens count the most. Always look at the tens first.

Compare the tens, then the ones

  1. Look at the tens. More tens means a greater number.
  2. Same tens? Look at the ones.
  3. Same tens and same ones? The numbers are equal.
Example

Compare 43 and 61.

Look at the tens. 43 has 4 tens. 61 has 6 tens. 6 tens is more.

Answer: 43 is less than 61

The symbols >, < and =

SymbolSayExample
>is greater than52 > 25
<is less than29 < 31
=is equal to30 + 6 = 36

The alligator trick: think of > and < as a hungry alligator mouth. The mouth is open toward the greater number, because it wants to eat more. The small point faces the smaller number.

On a number line, greater numbers are farther to the right.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Comparing the ones first: “29 > 31, because 9 > 1”Start with the tens: 2 tens < 3 tens, so 29 < 31
Counting all the pieces: 29 has more blocks than 31A ten is worth 10 ones. Count tens first
Thinking 36 and 63 are equalSame digits, different places: 36 < 63
Thinking 70 is like 770 is 7 tens. 7 is 7 ones. 70 > 7
Turning the symbol the wrong way: 52 < 25The open mouth faces the greater number: 52 > 25

faq.q: How do you compare two-digit numbers in 1st grade?
faq.a: Look at the tens first; the number with more tens is greater. If the tens are the same, compare the ones, and if both are the same, the numbers are equal.

faq.q: What is the alligator trick for greater than and less than?
faq.a: Think of > and < as an alligator mouth that always opens toward the greater number, because it wants to eat more. So 52 > 25 and 25 < 52.

faq.q: Why do kids think 29 is greater than 31?
faq.a: They see the big 9 or count more pieces. But 29 has only 2 tens and 31 has 3 tens, so 29 < 31.
No. They use the same digits, but 36 is 3 tens and 6 ones, and 63 is 6 tens and 3 ones. So 36 < 63.
